sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Welcome to our Acoustic Spectrogram and Video Tracking Laboratory. Adjust ground truth and predicted temporal boundaries in Tab 1 to monitor Temporal IoU. In Tab 2, click Inject Identity Switch to watch MOTA remain deceptively high at 90 percent while IDF1 exposes the fragmentation.

sentences.speaker: Kaito
sentences.text: Whoa, look at Tab 2, Dr. Nova! When I inject an Identity Switch, MOTA barely changes to 90 percent, while IDF1 crashes down to 80 percent!

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Active Checkpoint 1: Over 1,000 pedestrian ground truth detections, a tracker yields zero false positives and zero false negatives, yet exchanges two pedestrians' IDs 15 times. Why does MOTA stay at 98.5 percent while autonomous braking fails?

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Kaito, let's test whether engineers can diagnose the deceptive 98.5% MOTA paradox when two pedestrians swap tracking IDs 15 times!

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Spot on! MOTA adds identity switches into the numerator alongside single-frame detection errors, so 15 swaps across 1,000 frames yields 98.5 percent MOTA. Yet repeating ID swaps fracture Kalman velocity vectors, triggering phantom braking. IDF1 and HOTA expose this trajectory breakup cleanly.

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Not quite. Remember that MOTA does not exclude false detections or measure memory latency. The critical anomaly is mathematical weighting: each IDSW carries a tiny weight of 1 in the MOTA sum, hiding catastrophic track fragmentation that only IDF1 and HOTA's association term detect.

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: In the Tabular Knowledge Base Entity Linker Workbench, select ambiguous cells like Paris, Jordan, Apple, or missing-header Washington. Notice how row sibling attributes and ontological schema filtering drive Wikidata cosine similarity ranking past 0.94.

sentences.speaker: Kaito
sentences.text: With Chicago Bulls in the row context, Michael Jordan scores 0.96 cosine similarity over the country of Jordan, Dr. Nova!

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Active Checkpoint 2: A spreadsheet column header was stripped to Col_1, holding 'Washington' alongside Seattle, 120,000 Employees, and Founded 1994. How should the entity resolution engine disambiguate it cleanly?

sentences.speaker: Kaito
sentences.text: Without informative headers, can our entity linker still figure out 'Washington' using row attributes and ontology filtering? Select the best resolution!

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Excellent synthesis! Even when column headers vanish into Col_1, sibling row values constrain schema compatibility—disqualifying George Washington as schema Person—and contextual vector embeddings achieve high cosine similarity against matching corporate knowledge graph entries.

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Not quite. Guessing blindly by alphabetical order or dropping tables wastes enterprise assets. Neuro-symbolic disambiguation unites row-level sibling attributes, hard ontological type filtering, and contextual dense embedding similarity.
